pastey design

A Claude Code plugin that opens generated documents and copy/paste snippets in the user's editor automatically.

draft · created 2026-10-04 · backlog: B01

Goal

Anything Claude produces for a human to read or reuse opens in the user's editor of choice (VS Code by default) without being asked. Two kinds of output:

  • File output — specs, plans and other human-readable files Claude writes.
  • Pasteable text — SQL, command lines, config blocks and similar, which today exist only in chat.

Success: the user never scrolls the terminal or hunts for a path to read a document or copy a snippet.

Approach

One opening mechanism, one convention.

  • A Claude Code PostToolUse hook on Write and Edit runs an opener script that decides, deterministically, whether to open the written file.
  • A skill teaches Claude to save pasteable text as a snippet file, so the same hook opens it. Claude's only discretionary act is choosing to write a snippet; opening is never left to Claude.

Rejected: skill-instructions-only (non-deterministic: Claude forgets or over-opens) and a VS Code extension watching the filesystem (heavy, VS Code-only).

Packaging

A Claude Code plugin, so one install enables the skill and hook for every project.

.claude-plugin/plugin.json
hooks/hooks.json          PostToolUse, matcher Write|Edit → opener
skills/pastey/SKILL.md    snippet convention
scripts/pastey_open.py    the opener (Python, stdlib only, run with uv)
config/defaults.toml      default editor, allow and deny globs

Open item for the plan: confirm the plugin hook format (hooks/hooks.json, matcher and command variables) against current Claude Code documentation before implementing.

The opener

Reads the hook JSON from stdin (tool name, file path, session id). Always exits 0 and prints nothing, so it never blocks or clutters Claude.

  1. Normalize the path relative to the project root.
  2. Match deny first, then allow. No allow match → exit silently.
  3. Consult the session record (a JSON file in the temp dir keyed by session id, written atomically).
    • New file created by Write → open.
    • Edit or overwrite → open only if the file is not yet in the session record.
  4. Launch <editor> -r <path> (reuse the current window) and record the path.

The editor CLI cannot report open tabs, so "re-open only if not already open" is approximated by the session record: a tab the user closes mid-session stays closed until the next session.

Configuration

TOML, layered: plugin defaults ← ~/.pastey.toml (user) ← .pastey.toml (project).

  • editor — any command; default code.
  • allow / deny — globs relative to the project root.

Defaults:

  • allow: docs/**/*.md, snippets/**, README.md, the specs and plans directories.
  • deny: docs/site/**, docs/roadmap.md (generated, rewritten on every build).
  • Everything not allowed is denied, so source code never opens.
  • HTML is not allowed by default; a project opts in via .pastey.toml.

Snippet convention (the skill)

When Claude produces text the user will copy or run, it saves it with Write to snippets/NNNN-meaningful-name.<ext> inside the project:

  • NNNN is the next number, from the existing files in snippets/ (history is kept; nothing is overwritten).
  • The name says what the snippet does (0003-orders-by-region.sql).
  • The extension matches the content (.sql, .ps1, .sh, .json) for syntax highlighting.
  • Snippets are project artifacts and are kept, not temp files.
  • Claude also gives a one-line pointer in chat naming the file.

Errors

  • Editor not on PATH: log one line to %TEMP%\pastey\pastey.log; do nothing else.
  • Any unexpected exception: logged, exit 0.
  • Parallel or subagent writes: each file is its own invocation; the record is written atomically; a rare double open is harmless.

Testing

  • Unit tests: glob matching (deny before allow), layered config, open-once logic, with the editor launch injected and mocked.
  • End-to-end: pipe a sample hook payload into the script with a stub editor command that logs its arguments; assert it runs for an allowed path and not for a denied one.
  • Manual smoke test in a real Claude Code session: write a spec, write a snippet.

Non-goals

  • Opening source code or generated files by default.
  • Detecting open or closed editor tabs.
  • Opening text that never becomes a file, other than through the snippet convention.
